notes: old = before prefix optimization; new = initial prefix with incorrect directory-order assumption; corrected = bounded metadata sorting before prefix hydration.
The initial prefix binary is superseded for correctness. Its mixed warmup did not validate exact page IDs. None of its throughput figures qualify the corrected implementation.

The old mixed window completed 600 seconds before combined collection aborted on an unrecognized exact legacy HTTP 400 admission envelope. All 117 such errors remain errors; the raw unexpected_errors and complete fields are preserved. Together with 240 list refusals, this window failed.
The exact request-admission envelope was pinned by a failing then passing unit test. Other HTTP 400 node/disk errors stay unexpected; no errors are converted to successes.
The initial old server copy lacked executable mode and failed before load. This startup failure is retained separately and is not a QPS attempt.

Hidden layouts are specified in legacy string order. The earlier incorrect prefix scanned native length-prefixed order, so its 99-visible-gap batching was not the intended traversal. Corrected metadata sorting exposes that actual sequential gap.
CPU and allocations are shared-window totals, divided by successful requests; mixed endpoint costs are not individually attributed. Low-load hidden totals include background cluster work.

The old/new diagnosis uses frozen profile v1; corrected diagnosis and gate use profile v2. stress_diagnosis rates, durations and worker counts remain identical. The corrected harness also requires exact base-page identities and retains monotonic scheduling time.
All measured requests have no retry. Warm caches and zero active Channel runtimes are intentional. Local dirty ARM64 evidence does not qualify clean exact-tag Linux AMD64 publication.
